title: Korea Stock Market Today, Oct 28, 2026: KOSPI +6.63%, KOSDAQ +3.69% as SK hynix Record Results Lift Chip Stocks
content:
KOSPI closed at 6,012.44, up 6.63%, and KOSDAQ closed at 771.28, up 3.69%, after SK hynix reported record quarterly results and announced additional shareholder returns. KOSPI regained the 6,000 level during the session, and a buy-side sidecar was triggered at 9:54 a.m. Individual themes moved on their own news: chip equipment and back-end names, MLCC and substrate makers after Samsung Electro-Mechanics' outlook, humanoid robot stocks, cybersecurity stocks and optical transceiver names.

1. SK hynix posts record results — KOSPI jumps, buy-side sidecar triggered

SK hynix reported third-quarter revenue of 104.6155 trillion won and operating profit of 83.3338 trillion won, its highest ever. Growth was driven by higher sales of high-value AI memory such as HBM4 and server DDR5. It also announced an additional 60 trillion won in shareholder returns, which would bring this year's total to about 100 trillion won. Expectations for the chip cycle and buying in large-cap stocks lifted KOSPI back above 6,000 during the session, and a buy-side sidecar was triggered at 9:54 a.m. as KOSPI 200 futures surged. KOSPI closed at 6,012.44 (+6.63%) and KOSDAQ at 771.28 (+3.69%). Samsung Electronics (including the preferred shares), SK hynix, SK Telecom, SK, SK Square and Samsung Electro-Mechanics were in focus, and the strength in large chip stocks spread to related equipment and parts names.

2. Chip stocks — equipment, test and back-end names strengthen

Expectations for AI memory demand pulled buying across the chip value chain. More memory production and demand for high-performance chips supported sentiment toward manufacturing equipment as well as test, inspection and back-end processes. Names in focus: equipment and process names Wonik IPS, Tes, Jusung Engineering, PSK, STI and Cymechs; test, inspection and back-end names TFE, DoosanTesna, Okins Electronics, Intekplus, YC, DI and Neosem; and parts, memory and packaging names Haesung DS, Hanyang Digitech and Melcon.

3. Samsung Electro-Mechanics' MLCC outlook — parts and substrate stocks in focus

Samsung Electro-Mechanics said it expects record results, with large quarter-on-quarter growth from the first quarter of 2027, on rising demand for multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCC) used in AI data centers. It has signed or is negotiating long-term supply contracts for high-value MLCC with about 50 customers, and expects to lock in more than half of next year's MLCC sales through such contracts. Demand for high-capacity, high-voltage MLCC for AI servers and tightening supply are the main backdrop. MLCC and electronic parts names in focus were Hankem, Kochip and Amotech; substrate and PCB names were TLB, Simmtech, Korea Circuit and Daeduck Electronics. Being named in the theme does not mean these companies have direct supply contracts with Samsung Electro-Mechanics, and theme-driven buying is included.

4. Lee Jae-yong checks on the robot business — humanoid robot stocks strengthen

News that Samsung Electronics Chairman Lee Jae-yong visited the company's robot unit, the RX business promotion office, on the 27th to review humanoid robot development and commercialization drew attention. Samsung is reportedly working to refine precise manipulation technology and apply it first at manufacturing sites, and expectations rose that robots will be developed as a next growth driver. PNS Robotics, Zenix Robotics, Wonik Holdings, Hanla Cast, Rainbow Robotics, SPG and Robotis were in focus. Whether each company directly supplies Samsung Electronics, and the size of any actual orders, should be checked separately.

5. Hacking worries at financial firms — cybersecurity stocks in focus

Worries about information leaks and account takeovers grew on news that hacking incidents spread from banks to the brokerage industry. Expectations rose for stronger security systems and more spending on monitoring, authentication and network security at financial institutions. Genians, SP Soft, AhnLab, Xgate, Aton, Sands Lab, Raon Secure, Monitorapp, Hansak and ICTK were in focus. Theme-driven buying played a role, and the background differs by stock.

6. Bitgwajeonja (빛과전자) wins an initial optical transceiver order — optical communication stocks strengthen

Bitgwajeonja (빛과전자) hit its upper limit after saying it secured an initial mass-production order for 25Gbps optical transceivers from a U.S. optical communications company. Optical transceivers convert electrical signals to optical signals and are used in communication networks and data transfer infrastructure. The order raised hopes for entry into the U.S. market and expanded production. Bitsaem Electronics (빛샘전자), Gwangjeonja, Korea Advanced Materials, Mercury and Taihan Fiberoptics were also in focus. Bitgwajeonja' own order should be separated from the theme-driven gains in the other names.

Quick FAQ

How did KOSPI and KOSDAQ close on Oct 28?
KOSPI rose 6.63% to 6,012.44 and KOSDAQ rose 3.69% to 771.28. A buy-side sidecar was triggered on KOSPI at 9:54 a.m.

Why did Korean stocks surge?
SK hynix reported record third-quarter revenue and operating profit and announced an additional 60 trillion won in shareholder returns, drawing buying into large chip stocks.

Do all MLCC and substrate stocks supply Samsung Electro-Mechanics directly?
No. Being named in the theme does not mean a direct supply contract, and theme-driven buying is included.
